newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Trade in Slovenia SKB to resume on Jan 28.
newsitem.headline: Trade in Slovenia SKB to resume on Jan 28.

text.p: Trading in the shares of Slovenian bank SKB will resume on Tuesday following a one-week suspension, the Ljubljana bourse said on Monday.
"We received SKB's statement today and trade in its shares will resume tomorrow," Lidija Gabrijelcic, a spokeswoman at the bourse, told Reuters.
SKB shares were suspended from Tuesday last week as by the day before their average price had risen over 30 percent since the bank's last public announcement on the price of its shares.
Bourse regulations stipulate that trading be suspended after such a rise or fall until the company concerned issues a statement on why it thinks its share price has made such a move.

SKB said the move may have been influenced by its decision to issue global depositary receipts (GDR) which would represent up to 29 percent of SKB's capital and which will be listed on the London bourse in the middle of February.
Last week the Bank of Slovenia gave its accord to SKB's listing abroad by giving the green light to increase the maximum foreign shareholding in SKB to 49 percent from 30 percent.

"Due to the foreign listing, shares of SKB could well gain by 10 percent tomorrow, which is the bourse's regulated daily limit," said Nina Jarc, a trader at Nova Ljubljanska banka, adding SKB could continue surging for weeks.
